events.feedback:
This draft for the Yellow-rumped Warbler (Setophaga coronata) is exceptionally solid. The facts are completely accurate, the local seasonal timeline makes perfect sense, and the tone is exactly where it needs to be for a general public guide—engaging without being overly dramatic.

A critical review with an absolute zero-mistake lens reveals only one technical layout correction regarding the scientific name, and a tiny punctuation observation:

Technical Layout Correction
Scientific Name Typography: In the main header line, the genus and species name is currently formatted in bold text: Setophaga coronata. In botanical and zoological publishing, scientific names must always be italicized to meet professional standards. Changing this to bold-italicized or simply italicized text (*Setophaga coronata*) will make it perfectly air-tight and keep the park director happy.

Content & Layout Check
The Wax Myrtle Fact: Stating they are the only warbler that can digest the waxy coating on bayberr
events.summary: Applied the reviewer's single actionable correction: the scientific name is now italicized (*Setophaga coronata*) to meet standard botanical and zoological typography conventions. No content, facts, structure, or other fields were altered.
